entities.name: Bobo of S. Teodoro
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Cardinal Bobo of S. Teodoro, a prominent figure in the Roman Curia during the late 12th century, served as a cardinal deacon and played a direct role in the complex political and ecclesiastical landscape of the nascent Papal States. Elevated to the College of Cardinals by Pope Celestine III around 1193, Bobo's career unfolded during a period of intense papal consolidation of power and diplomatic maneuvering across Europe. His significance lies in his participation in crucial papal elections and his involvement in the administrative and diplomatic machinery that shaped the medieval papacy's growing influence, particularly as it transitioned towards the powerful pontificate of Innocent III.

Bobo of S. Teodoro's primary activities centered on his duties within the College of Cardinals. He was created cardinal deacon of San Teodoro, a title he held until his death on October 16, 1199. A notable event in his career was his participation in the papal election of January 8, 1198, which resulted in the unanimous election of Cardinal Lothar of Segni, who became Pope Innocent III. This election was pivotal, ushering in one of the most impactful pontificates of the Middle Ages, and Bobo's presence underscored the continuity and evolving structure of the Church's highest deliberative body. He also served as an auditor, settling disputes and administering justice within the Curia.

His brief but active tenure as cardinal contributed to the administrative continuity and the decision-making processes that buttressed papal authority in a volatile era. Bobo's involvement in the election of Innocent III, specifically, connects him to the very foundation of a papacy that would significantly expand its temporal and spiritual claims, leaving an indelible mark on European politics, law, and culture. The collective actions of cardinals like Bobo ensured the smooth succession of popes and the ongoing governance of the universal Church, even as internal and external pressures mounted.
